title: JD Vance top opposition
follower_snapshot_pt: November 18, 2026, Pacific Time, from X public metrics on accounts that were opened (Levin, Hammer, Shipwreckedcrew and the three new entries refreshed this morning); Loomer, koshercockney and Pino Americano refreshed again at the Walsh poll close (about 11:35 AM PT); Nov 19, 2026: Thiessen, Hammer, and the two new entries (MeidasTouch, ImBreckWorsham) refreshed from X public metrics; Nov 20, 2026: Levin, MeidasTouch, Thiessen, and the four new entries (Shapiro, Krassenstein, Medvin, Rothman) refreshed from X public metrics; Nov 21, 2026: MeidasTouch, FactPost, and the five new entries (Filipkowski, Hanson, Meiselas, el-Baghdadi, GOP Ls) refreshed from X public metrics; Nov 23, 2026: the five new entries (Jones, Marshall, Erickson, Cotto, Priorities USA) from X public metrics; Nov 24, 2026: Loomer, Levin, Thiessen and the six new entries (Cuomo, Hayes, Singal, Baker, Friedman, Brattani) from X public metrics; Nov 25, 2026: Loomer, Erickson and the four new entries (Stein, Armstrong, Holt, Hanania) from X public metrics; Nov 26, 2026: Krassenstein and the seven new entries (Rupar, Cole, Oates, Decoding Fox News, Watson, LanaQuest, Asuka Groyper) from X public metrics
ranking_method: Ranked by reach and frequency. Score = rank_reach × (1 + 0.25 × (critical_items − 1)). rank_reach is the opened X follower count, except for CUFI Action Fund, where rank_reach is the parent @CUFI follower count (56,979), which is disclosed in that entry. Ties break by raw followers, then name.

side_labels.right: Conservative or Republican-aligned officials, commentators, and outlets
side_labels.left: Democratic or liberal-aligned officials and commentators
side_labels.institutional: Organizations or newspapers that are not primarily a U.S. party office (used here for ADL and The Jerusalem Post)
side_labels.unspecified: Used only when the account bio and opened posts do not state a partisan identity (FactPost; Deborah Lipstadt; Ed Krassenstein; İyad el-Baghdadi; GOP Ls)

sources.a: Authors of critical items already in entries.json
sources.b: Prominent accounts in replies and quote-posts under those items, including the Matt Walsh poll thread of November 17–18, 2026, and the Brian Kilmeade clip of November 18, 2026; the Nov 18–19 NYT-report relays and the Thiessen/Hemingway thread; Nov 19–20 Emerson-poll, Axios Israel-poll, and Bolton-clip threads; Nov 20–21 White House briefing threads (Radel/Iran-war answer, Trump’s 'statement was fine' remarks) and the 'stupid wars' anniversary posts; Nov 22 threads under the Newsmax and StrawPoll.us poll posts, the People’s Poll post, the Brazil/Rockbridge post, and the Mossadil Iran clip; Nov 23 threads and quotes under Byron York’s early-state poll post, the Alex Jones Royce White post, Erick Erickson’s VP-history post, the Trump Daily Posts unity-ticket relay, the @VP Nvidia post, and Gunther Eagleman’s Oversight post; Nov 20–23 Ann Coulter “People’s Choice, Stephen Miller” post and comparison threads (Ed Krassenstein briefing clip, S.E. Cupp and Jenna Ellis quotes, Jon Cooper, Roman Sheremeta); Nov 24 threads and quotes under Reuters’ Vitol-probe post, Laura Loomer’s Masad-meeting post, David M. Friedman’s Tucker post, Vance’s “Welcome back Jensen” post, Chris Cuomo’s quote, the @whitesocksAF Tucker clip, Mario Nawfal’s Nvidia post, and the OSZ CNN-ranking post; Nov 25 threads and quotes under Laura Loomer’s Masad/El-Sayed and “Called it again” posts, Cynthia Holt’s El-Sayed post, Sam Stein’s focus-group post, Richard Hanania’s Miller post, the @VP deportation post, and replies under the Szypula, Nawfal, Erickson, Drop Site and C14 posts; Nov 26 threads and quotes under Aaron Rupar’s Iowa clips, @JDVance’s Stephen Miller credit post, the @VP Iowa clip, and posts by Eric Daugherty and LanaQuest
sources.c: A fresh X and web search for high-reach Vance critics on the right and the left

exclusions: Matt Walsh is not listed. His November 17 thread asked about 'raw political talent' and included Vance in a poll; he did not attack Vance. The thread is in the tracker as mixed.

Tomi Lahren (@TomiLahren, 2,865,615 followers) commented in the Walsh thread that she wanted someone who 'stays true to the values' and named Ron DeSantis. That is a preference, not a critique of Vance, so she is not listed.
Sen. Tom Cotton was described in Jewish Insider as taking a 'veiled swipe' at Vance over Iran policy without naming him. Because the opened reporting says he did not name Vance, he is not listed.
Ryan Schmelz of Fox News reported Fine's comments; he is a correspondent, not a critic, and his account is under the follower threshold.

News outlets that only reported criticism (Fox News news article, JTA news reports, Jewish Insider news reports) are not listed as critics. Signed editorials, signed columns, and organizational statements are.

Jeremy Barr (@jeremymbarr, 29,080 followers), media reporter for The Guardian, quoted the Kilmeade clip calling it 'one of the strongest critiques I've seen in a while.' That is a reporter's observation, not a critique, so he is not listed.

John Daniel Davidson (@johnddavidson, 39,716; senior editor at The Federalist) and Douglass Mackey (@douglassmackey, 79,635) quoted the Kilmeade clip to push back on Kilmeade, not Vance; they are not critics of Vance.
Steve Cortes (@SteveCortes, 536,581) posted a supportive counter to Kilmeade; he is in the tracker as supportive, not on this list.

Ryan Fournier (@RyanAFournier, 1,280,313; founder of Students for Trump) and Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone, 1,979,031) relayed the Nov 18 NYT report without their own critique in the opened text, so they are not listed. Fournier's relay is in the tracker as an item.

Acyn (@Acyn, 800,179) posted the Trump MOU clip with a reporter's question about Vance; that is a clip caption, not a critique, so Acyn is not listed. Eyal Yakoby (@EYakoby, 317,472) posted the MOU clip without naming Vance; not listed.
Mollie Hemingway (@MZHemingway, 1,504,229) defended Vance on Nov 19; she is in the tracker as supportive, not on this list.

Ryan Fournier (@RyanAFournier, 1,280,274) relayed the RCP 2028 average (Nov 20) and a John Bolton clip (Nov 19) without his own critique in the opened text; both posts are tracker items, but he is not listed. John Bolton (@AmbJohnBolton, 847,967; former National Security Advisor) said in the relayed clip that Vance 'has crossed a line' with Trump; that is an assessment of the Trump–Vance relationship, not a critique of Vance's record, so he is not listed.
The New York Post's Nov 19 post on the Emerson poll is a headline relay by a news outlet; it is a tracker item but the Post is not listed as a critic.

Jon Michael Raasch (@JMRaasch, 13,417; Daily Mail White House correspondent) posted the most-viewed clip of Vance’s Nov 20 Iran-war answer (1.08M views), noting 'Trump doesn’t look stoked'; he is a reporter under the follower threshold and is not listed.

Ed Krassenstein’s Nov 20 post that Trump “seemingly endorsed Stephen Miller for President over JD Vance and Marco Rubio” (4,266,117 views when re-opened Nov 23) is commentary on Trump, not a critique of Vance, so it does not add a critical item to his entry. It is logged as a mixed tracker item.
Newsmax’s Nov 22 “RUBIO LEADS EARLY” post and Trump Daily Posts’ Nov 22 StrawPoll.us result are headline or poll relays; both are tracker items, but neither account is listed as a critic.

TMK (@themagaking, 79,445) posted results of his own unscientific “People’s Poll” on Nov 22 (Vance last at 7%) after posting a supportive Vance item on Nov 20; both are tracker items, but he is not listed pending a direct critique.
Derrick Evans (@DerrickEvans4WV, 865,929; former WV House member) quoted Newsmax on Nov 22 to say he will never vote for Rubio; that is not a critique of Vance, so he is not listed.
Byron York (@ByronYork, 580,384; Washington Examiner) reported the OnMessage early-state poll on Nov 23; it is a tracker item, but as a reporting relay he is not listed as a critic.

Rep. Robert Garcia (incoming House Oversight chair) reportedly sent document letters that include Vance (per Gunther Eagleman’s Nov 22 post); the letters and Garcia’s own posts were not opened, so he is not listed.
S.E. Cupp (@secupp, 428,655) quoted Ann Coulter’s Nov 20 Miller post to mock the idea; that is not a critique of Vance, so she is not listed.

Jenna Ellis (@realJennaEllis, 1,132,322; senior policy adviser at the American Family Association, per bio) quoted Coulter, “Let’s really not”; that is a rejection of the Miller pitch, not a critique of Vance, so she is not listed.
Jon Cooper (@joncoopertweets, 1,372,161) wrote that Coulter wants Republicans to nominate Miller and called that “pathetic”; the attack is on Miller and the GOP, not on Vance, so he is not listed.

Roman Sheremeta (@rshereme, 99,840) said he wants Miller to run, citing Trump’s “better than these two guys” briefing joke; that is a preference, not a critique of Vance’s record, so he is not listed.

Reuters (@Reuters) and Bloomberg (@business) reported the Nov 23 Senate (Hassan) inquiry into Vance and Vitol; as news reporting they are not listed as critics. Sen. Maggie Hassan’s own letter and posts on it were not opened, so she is not listed.
OSZ (@OpenSourceZone, 60,953) relayed the CNN/Harry Enten 2028 ranking; as a poll relay it is a tracker item but not listed as a critic.
Dan Burmawi (@DanBurmawy, 141,926; CEO of IDI Center) posted about Amjad Masad after his meeting with Vance; the criticism targets Masad, not Vance, so he is not listed.
America First (@ImperiumFirst, 86,967) mocked Tucker Carlson’s pro-Vance remark; the jab is at Carlson, so the account is not listed.
Drop Site News (@DropSiteNews, 499,172) reported on Loomer’s campaign against Amjad Masad; logged as a supportive counter, not a critic.
Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal, 3,992,718) relayed the Senate Vitol inquiry; as a news relay it is a tracker item but not listed as a critic.
Paul A. Szypula (@Bubblebathgirl, 382,768) prefers Rubio but calls Vance “fine”; logged as mixed, not listed.

Fox News Digital’s Nov 25 report on House Republicans urging Rubio to run is news reporting; the quoted members (Malliotakis, Stutzman, Gimenez, Haridopolos) praised Rubio without criticizing Vance, so they are not listed.
Dr. Eli David (@DrEliDavid, 860,688) posted about Amjad Masad without mentioning Vance; not listed.
Stephen Robinson (@SER1897, 10,986; Public Notice writer) wrote the most-liked quote of Rupar’s clip (8,422 likes) but is below 50,000 and not tied to a major organization; not listed.
David Axelrod and Chuck Todd were quoted criticizing the Obama remark in The Daily Beast (Nov 26); their X posts were not opened this update, so they are not listed.
@Acyn (798,547; senior digital editor) posted a clip of Vance’s remarks without commentary; not listed as a critic.
This list is not exhaustive. A missing name is not a finding that the person is not a critic.
